tooltip.title: Treatment by Stage
tooltip.markdown: CTCL treatment follows a stage-adapted approach. Early-stage disease is managed with skin-directed therapies, while advanced disease requires systemic agents. The goal is long-term disease control, not cure.

tooltip.title: Early-Stage Mycosis Fungoides (Stage IA to IIA)
tooltip.markdown: Primary goal is symptom palliation using skin-directed therapies.

tooltip.title: Stage IA Management
tooltip.markdown: Focus on clearing limited skin lesions with minimal toxicity. "Watchful waiting" is an option for asymptomatic disease.

tooltip.title: First-Line Therapies for Stage IA
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Topical Corticosteroids:** High-potency steroids are often the initial choice.
-   **Topical Mechlorethamine:** An alternative first-line option.
-   **Phototherapy (NB-UVB):** For widespread but thin patches.

tooltip.title: Refractory/Localized Stage IA Lesions
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Localized Radiation:** Highly effective for a single resistant plaque.
-   **Topical Retinoids/Imiquimod:** Options for persistent localized disease.

tooltip.title: Stage IB / IIA Management
tooltip.markdown: Requires therapies that can cover larger skin surface areas. Systemic therapy may be added for refractory disease.

tooltip.title: Primary Therapies for Stage IB/IIA
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Phototherapy (PUVA):** Preferred for thicker, more extensive plaques due to deeper penetration.
-   **TSEBT (Total Skin Electron Beam):** Low-dose (10-12 Gy) is effective for widespread plaques.

tooltip.title: Refractory or Systemic Options for IB/IIA
tooltip.markdown: -   **Bexarotene or Methotrexate:** Can be added to skin-directed therapies.

tooltip.title: Advanced-Stage Mycosis Fungoides (Stage IIB to IV)
tooltip.markdown: Requires systemic therapy, often in combination with skin-directed treatments.

tooltip.title: Stage IIB Management
tooltip.markdown: Focus on controlling tumors and systemic spread.

tooltip.title: First-Line for Stage IIB
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Skin-directed plus systemic therapy:** Tumor-stage disease is rarely controlled by skin-directed therapy alone; combine skin-directed treatment with a systemic agent chosen by disease burden, comorbidity and goals.
-   **Local radiation:** Highly effective for limited tumors (single or few lesions), including low-dose palliative regimens.
-   **TSEBT:** Preferred for generalized tumors or extensive plaque/tumor disease; low-dose courses can be repeated.
-   **Systemic biologic-response modifiers:** Bexarotene (with lipid and thyroid monitoring), interferon-alpha and low-dose methotrexate are first-line systemic options, often combined with phototherapy or TSEBT.
-   **Brentuximab vedotin:** For CD30-expressing MF after at least one prior systemic therapy; consider early for large-cell transformation.
-   **Mogamulizumab:** FDA-approved for relapsed or refractory MF/SS after at least one prior systemic therapy; not an unrestricted first-line option.
-   **Clinical trial** enrollment is encouraged at every line.

tooltip.title: Stage III Management
tooltip.markdown: Management is similar to Sézary Syndrome.

tooltip.title: First-Line for Stage III
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Gentle skin care:** Emollients and low- to mid-potency topical corticosteroids; aggressive skin-directed therapy can worsen a compromised barrier.
-   **Phototherapy-based combinations:** PUVA (or NB-UVB) combined with interferon-alpha or bexarotene; low-dose TSEBT is an option for symptomatic generalized disease.
-   **Extracorporeal photopheresis (ECP):** Preferred for erythrodermic disease, especially with blood involvement (B1/B2); usually combined with interferon-alpha or bexarotene.
-   **Systemic biologic-response modifiers:** Interferon-alpha, bexarotene or low-dose methotrexate, alone or with ECP/phototherapy.
-   **Later-line targeted agents:** Mogamulizumab after at least one prior systemic therapy (most active in blood); brentuximab vedotin for CD30-expressing disease after prior systemic therapy.
-   **Avoid initial multi-agent chemotherapy:** Responses are short and infection risk is high in erythrodermic patients.

tooltip.title: Stage IV Management
tooltip.markdown: Palliative intent. Focus on quality of life.

tooltip.title: First-Line for Stage IV
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Systemic therapy is the backbone:** Nodal (IVA2) and visceral (IVB) disease need systemic treatment rather than skin-directed therapy alone. Preferred targeted agents: mogamulizumab (after at least one prior systemic therapy; most active in blood and skin), brentuximab vedotin for CD30-expressing disease, and HDAC inhibitors (romidepsin, vorinostat).
-   **Single-agent chemotherapy:** Gemcitabine, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin or pralatrexate for progressive disease; multi-agent regimens are reserved for transformed or rapidly progressive visceral disease because responses are brief.
-   **Allogeneic HSCT:** The only potentially curative option; refer eligible patients early, ideally after achieving a response (reduced-intensity conditioning is typical).
-   **Palliative radiation and skin care:** Local radiation for symptomatic tumors or nodes, low-dose TSEBT for extensive skin disease, and continued barrier care with infection surveillance.
-   **Clinical trial** enrollment is strongly preferred.

tooltip.title: Sézary Syndrome Management
tooltip.markdown: Requires aggressive systemic therapy targeting the high burden of disease in the blood.

tooltip.title: First-Line for Sézary Syndrome
tooltip.markdown:
-   **ECP-based multimodality therapy (preferred first-line):** Extracorporeal photopheresis, usually combined with interferon-alpha and/or bexarotene plus skin-directed therapy (topical corticosteroids, phototherapy).
-   **Mogamulizumab:** FDA-approved for relapsed or refractory Sézary syndrome after at least one prior systemic therapy; superior progression-free survival versus vorinostat in MAVORIC, with the highest response rates in blood.
-   **Low-dose alemtuzumab:** For refractory blood-predominant disease; requires CMV monitoring and infection prophylaxis.
-   **Allogeneic HSCT:** Consider in eligible patients after achieving a response, as the only potentially curative approach.
-   **Avoid initial multi-agent chemotherapy:** Responses are short-lived and infection risk is high.
